# Distributed Task and Phase Feedback (Provisional)

## Scope and Coordinate Convention

F02 (#11786) implements a local controller for a forward-dynamics plant. It
consumes an already fitted nominal state and actuator feedforward trajectory,
plus time-varying LQR gains from the existing MOSAIC provider. It does not
identify body parameters, integrate a plant, fit motion capture, or qualify an
engine. The configuration difference adapter returns
$e_q=\operatorname{difference}(q,q^*)\in\mathbb R^{n_v}$ with a **current minus
reference** sign; $e_v=v-v^*$. This remains meaningful when $n_q\ne n_v$.
The adapter supplies the tangent inverse mass $M(q)^{-1}$ and must be native to
the chosen model. The Euclidean unit-mass adapter is restricted to analytic
fixtures. The controller rejects nonfinite states and nonsymmetric or
nonpositive inverse mass matrices.

For time interval $[t_k,t_{k+1})$, the frozen nominal input $u_k^{\rm ff}$ and
MOSAIC gain $K_k\in\mathbb R^{n_u\times 2n_v}$ produce

$$
u_k^{\rm requested}=u_k^{\rm ff}+u_k^{\rm task}
  -P_k K_k\begin{bmatrix}e_q\\e_v\end{bmatrix}.
$$

The task term is calculated from named, framed and unit-labeled pelvis/feet,
trunk, arms, wrists/hands and club targets. Each task has an explicit phase
mask and priority. For task Jacobian $J_i$ and position-error adapter
$d_i(y_i^*,y_i)$, its local feedback wrench is
$w_i=k_{p,i}d_i+k_{d,i}(\dot y_i^*-\dot y_i)$.
The one-to-one actuator selection $S$ maps a task wrench to candidate actuator
effort $SJ_i^Tw_i$. Higher-priority task influence uses
$A_i=J_iM^{-1}S^T$; the lower-priority projector is updated by
$P\leftarrow P(I-(AP)^\dagger AP)$. Equal-priority terms share one level and
can compete; this is a local linearized control rule, not a guarantee of
global nonlinear tracking or disturbance rejection.

## Applied Input and Contact Boundary

Only an explicit unit-constant, one-to-one actuator-to-generalized-effort map
is supported. Generalized root coordinates are excluded from actuators. An
engine with a state-dependent transmission, muscle activation, or different
command-to-effort map requires a separate adapter and replay proof. The
controller reports the frozen feedforward, feedback correction, total
requested input, and post-limit **applied actuator torque** separately.
Direct allocation is admitted only for declared contact-free plants and
applies position-independent bounds and slew limits once per integration step.

The existing contact/grip QP can predict feasible actuator torques and
reactions only when an engine adapter supplies own-contact kinematics and a
native inverse-dynamics target $M\dot v+h$. Root slack or a hidden residual
drive is rejected. Predicted ground/grip reactions are diagnostics; they are
**not** injected into the native plant as measured external forces. Native
contact and grip reactions remain outputs of the forward solver. This QP
adapter has no full-body scientific qualification yet.

The caller samples the controller once at each integration-step boundary and
holds the applied torque exactly across that step. Steps start at the nominal
clock, remain contiguous, and cannot cross a policy boundary. The implemented
information pattern is exact simulated full state; estimated, delayed,
noisy, or measured-mocap feedback is unsupported. Independent open-loop replay
must load the resulting applied-torque history into a fresh plant with no
feedback or state resets under the F01 comparison and Tools T01 policies.

## Evidence and Limits

The analytic double-integrator test uses MOSAIC Riccati gains: the declared
restoring sign reduces a 0.4 rad initial error below 0.1 rad over 1.6 s, while
the reversed sign fails that bound. Other unit fixtures test phase masks,
priority conflict, wrapped-angle task errors, $n_q\ne n_v$ tangent errors,
actuator permutation, root-drive rejection, saturation and slew limits,
contact-QP feasibility, and failure without native contact dynamics. A
native one-joint MuJoCo motor test applies the saved torque to one forward
step without prescribing coordinates. These are software and local-control
checks, not proof of six-engine parity, full-swing capture matching, native
human contact validity, muscle-driven matching, or independent replay.

Reproduce the bounded evidence with
`python -m pytest tests/unit/motion_matching/test_distributed_feedback.py -q`.
The model/provider hashes, private capture identities, full-horizon replay,
observability, actuator internal state, measured contact and qualification
receipts remain open. The calculation registry and manual release stay blocked.
